resources.string: By downloading the code-switching model you agree to the Hebrish terms of use: free for personal, research, education and non-profit use; commercial use, including telephony, needs a licence.

The Hebrish models are free for personal, research, education and non-profit use. Commercial use, including telephony and call centres, needs a commercial licence: access@hebrish.app. Hebrish is experimental and trained on one speaker\'s voice; transcripts can be wrong, so check them before relying on them. It is provided as is, without warranty. Your audio stays on this phone.
Voice typing in English that gets the Hebrew words right. It all runs on your phone; your voice never leaves it.
Delete %1$s from this phone? You can download it again later.
Download failed: %1$s. Tap Download to resume.
Checking Hugging Face for a newer model…
Update available: %1$s (%2$d MB). %3$s stays in use until the new model is downloaded and verified, then it is deleted.
Needed to hear you. Audio never leaves the phone.
Not enabled yet. Turn on “Hebrish” in the system keyboard list.
Use HeliBoard as your main keyboard. Its mic key opens Hebrish, and once the text is in you are taken back to HeliBoard. In HeliBoard: Settings → Toolbar (or Preferences) → show the voice input key.
Return to previous keyboard after inserting
Tap here, switch to Hebrish, and speak…

Using the code-switching model? Its website has the results and every model, dataset and demo. Report a bug, ask for a feature or send feedback by email to feedback@hebrish.app, suggest a Hebrew word it gets wrong, or send voice samples to help it learn more voices.
No email app found. Write to %1$s.
Paused at %1$d:%2$02d. Resume, or tap ■ to insert.
Take discarded. Tap the mic to speak.
No text field to type into. Tap a field, then Insert last.
Password field: Hebrish doesn\'t dictate passwords. Switch to your regular keyboard.
Tap a text field first, then Insert last.
Automatic: the keyboard you came from (now %1$s)
Automatic: the keyboard you came from
Long-press the keyboard key in Hebrish to open the system keyboard picker at any time.
Model not downloaded. Tap the mic to open setup.
Microphone not granted. Tap the mic to open setup.
Too short. Tap the mic to try again.
Heard nothing. Tap the mic to try again.

Shows a floating microphone over other apps. Tap it to dictate into the text field you are in, without switching keyboards. Hebrish reads the focused text field only to put your transcript in at the cursor, and it never reads password fields. Audio and text stay on this phone.

A mic button that floats over every app. Tap it in any text field, talk, and tap Stop: the text goes in at the cursor and your keyboard stays as it is. While you talk it shows Pause, Retake and Discard. If no text field had focus when the text was ready, the mic shows Insert: tap a field, then Insert. Long-press the idle mic to insert the last transcript again. In the way? Double-tap it to shrink it to a small dot; tap the dot to bring it back. It runs as an accessibility service.
The floating mic is on. Drag it to move it, also while you talk (by the mic or the bar), or set its place below.
The floating mic is off. Turn on “Hebrish floating mic” in Accessibility settings, under Downloaded apps (or Installed apps). The guide below goes through it step by step.
Show only while a text field is focused
Insert the transcript into the focused text field
No text field to type into. Tap one, then tap Insert on the mic. The text is on the clipboard too.
Tap a text field first, then Insert.
Turn it on: step by step
Left or right edge: the mic snaps to that edge when you drag it. Anywhere: it stays exactly where you drop it.
Bar background while you talk: %1$d%% opaque
While you talk the mic is always red.
Long takes, type as you go and ALL CAPS are set on the Dictation screen.
It also needs the microphone: see the guide.
This field doesn\'t accept dictation; the text is on the clipboard.
Long takes, typing as you talk, ALL CAPS, history export
%1$s is not downloaded yet. Tap to download.
On. Opens from your keyboard\'s mic key.
Off. Optional: a mic over every app.

Each family is what a model is trained for; under it are its variants, from most accurate to fastest, with who each one is for. Sabich is the one to start with. Models download once and then work offline; you can keep several and switch any time. Speed and accuracy dots are estimates.
Not in this app yet. Runs on: %1$s
Waiting: downloads after the current one.
New versions of downloaded models are looked for when the app opens, at most every 6 hours. A model being updated stays usable until the new version is downloaded and checked.
A voice keyboard that opens from your regular keyboard\'s mic key, records, types the text in and switches back.
Done: the floating mic is on.
The floating mic is off. Go through the steps below; each button opens the right settings page, and this screen updates when you come back.
Open Accessibility settings, then Downloaded apps (on some phones Installed apps or Installed services), then Hebrish floating mic. Turn it on and tap Allow. If that works, skip to the last step.

Android 13 and later block accessibility for apps installed from an APK. Trying step 1 once shows a “Restricted setting” message; after that, open App info, tap ⋮ (top right), then Allow restricted settings, and confirm with your PIN or fingerprint. The ⋮ item only appears after that first try.
Back in Accessibility settings → Downloaded apps → Hebrish floating mic, the switch now works. Turn it on and tap Allow.
The floating mic records with the app\'s microphone permission.

Some phones (OnePlus, Xiaomi, Samsung and others) stop background apps to save battery, and the floating mic disappears until you turn it on again. Allow Hebrish to run unrestricted. On OnePlus, also check App info → Battery → Unrestricted.
Battery: optimised. Android may stop the floating mic.
A mic now sits at the edge of the screen. Tap into a text field, tap the mic, talk, and tap it again. Drag it to move it.

Takes can run up to %1$d minutes. While you talk, each stretch of speech is transcribed at the next pause, so when you tap stop only the last few seconds are left to do. The keyboard, the floating mic and Try it all work this way.

Off: the whole take goes in when you tap stop, and Discard throws all of it away. On: each part goes in as soon as it is transcribed, so long dictations appear while you talk; Discard then only drops the part not yet typed.
Everything you dictate is typed in capitals, in the keyboard, the floating mic and Try it. Just for fun. Applies from your next take.

Every take is kept on this phone with its text, length, model and how long it took to transcribe. Nothing is uploaded. Export it as a CSV file to save it to Google Drive, Downloads or anywhere the file picker offers.
%1$d takes kept on this phone (since version 0.8.1).

The CSV has one row per take: time, text, words, audio seconds, model, where you dictated, and the transcription timings (decode time, real-time factor, wait after stop) with the device and app version. Same first columns as the desktop app\'s history export.
No takes in the history yet.
This phone has no file picker to save the CSV with.
Delete every take in the history on this phone? This cannot be undone.

The model is loaded once and kept in memory. The floating mic loads it as soon as a text field gets focus, so it is ready by the time you tap. Silence at the start and end of a take is skipped. The very first take after the phone restarts still waits a few seconds for the model to load.
If the text has nowhere to go

Floating mic: if no text field has focus when the text is ready, the mic shows Insert. Tap a field, then Insert, and the text goes in at the cursor. It is on the clipboard too. Voice keyboard: Insert last transcript does the same.

Installed from an APK? An APK doesn\'t update itself. Hebrish has its own F-Droid repository: add it once, and every new version arrives as an ordinary app update. It is the same app, signed with the same key, so F-Droid updates this install and keeps your models and settings. It also works in Droid-ify and Neo Store.
1. Install F-Droid, if you don\'t have it
F-Droid asks to add the repository: confirm. Then search F-Droid for Hebrish. New releases reach the repository within six hours.
No F-Droid app found. Opening the repository in the browser.
In F-Droid: Settings → Repositories → +, then enter this address:
with this fingerprint (filled in for you by the button above):
This link always gives the newest APK. Install it over this one to update; you keep your models and settings.
Try it now: no setup needed
See what it does before you set it up as a keyboard.
Tap the mic, say a sentence, then tap again to stop. The text appears below. Nothing leaves your phone.

resources.string: Read it aloud: tap the mic first.
Your words land here. You can edit them, then copy or share.
Set it up for every app
Loading the model… (a few seconds, the first time only)
Download a model on the Models screen first (about 660 MB, one time).
Ready. Tap the mic and talk.
Done: %1$.1f s of audio; the text was ready %2$.1f s after you tapped stop. Tap the mic for more.
Didn\'t catch any words. Try again a bit closer to the mic.
That was very short. Tap, talk, then tap again.
The app needs microphone access to hear you.
Beeps, which mic to use, and Bluetooth buttons

Some apps, WhatsApp among them, report their grey placeholder as real text, so dictation would land after it. With this on, a short line with the cursor at its very start is treated as a placeholder and replaced. Turn it off if it ever replaces a word you typed.
Microphone: %1$s. Tap to switch between Bluetooth and the phone\'s mic.
No Bluetooth or headset mic is connected.
Beep when a take starts, stops, is retaken or discarded
Start: a rising pip. Stop: a falling pip. Retake: a quick double pip. Discard: a low pip.
Automatic always uses a Bluetooth headset mic when one is connected, then a wired or USB headset, then the phone\'s mic.
The mic in use is shown while you record. While a Bluetooth mic is in use, the headset switches to call audio, so music in it sounds worse until the take ends.
Bind a key on a Bluetooth shutter remote, a keyboard or a media remote to an action. Tap Learn, then press the key.
Buttons and intents work through the floating mic: turn it on first.

Only bound keys are taken; every other key works as before. Many camera shutter remotes send Volume up: binding it means the volume up key dictates instead. If Learn does nothing, turn the floating mic off and on again in Accessibility settings.
Apps such as Key Mapper, Tasker and MacroDroid can send these broadcast intents (package app.hebrish.dictation, no extras):
Full reference and examples: docs/external-control.md in the Hebrish-App repository on GitHub.
The lexicon, how to contribute, version

Hebrish is voice typing for people who speak English with Hebrew words in it: teudat zehut, arnona, be\'ezrat Hashem. The models are fine-tuned versions of NVIDIA Parakeet, and they run entirely on your phone. Hebrish is free and not-for-profit.
Every Hebrew word the models were taught, with what it means and how it is spelled. Browse it on hebrish.app.
Hebrish gets better with more voices and more words. Record a few sentences, suggest a word it gets wrong, or support the project.
Recognition runs on the phone. Audio is never uploaded.
Work down the list. Each button opens the right settings page; come back here when you\'re done and the step ticks itself off.
%1$d of %2$d steps done. Tap to continue.
Hebrish needs it to hear you. Audio stays on the phone.
Sabich (English with Hebrew words and tech vocabulary) is recommended. About 660 MB, once; use Wi-Fi.
Switch on Hebrish in your keyboard settings. Then the mic key on Hebrish Keyboard or HeliBoard opens it. You need this or the floating mic, or both.
A mic over every app, so you keep your usual keyboard. Android 13+ asks you to allow restricted settings first; the guide walks you through it.
Let Hebrish run unrestricted on battery, so the phone doesn\'t stop it in the background.
Turn off \"Pause app activity if unused\"
Otherwise Android takes the microphone permission away if you don\'t open the app for a few months. On the page that opens, switch it off.
Tap, talk, tap again. No keyboard setup needed for this.
Before you turn on the floating mic
The floating mic uses Android\'s accessibility service. This screen says what that lets Hebrish do and what Hebrish does with it.

Which text field has focus, and the editable fields in the window on screen. Hebrish uses this only to show the mic while you are in a text field and to put your transcript in at the cursor. It never reads or writes password fields.
It shows the mic button over other apps and types the text you dictated into the field. It acts only when you tap the mic or one of its buttons, never on its own.

It also sees hardware key presses, so a Bluetooth remote or keyboard key can start and stop takes. It acts only on keys you bind on the Sound, microphone and buttons screen; every other key passes through untouched.
Nowhere. Audio, transcripts and what is in your text fields stay on this phone. Nothing is collected, sent or shared. Privacy policy: hebrish.app/privacy.
Names, brands and Hebrew words, written your way

Words you want written your way: names, brands, Hebrew words in the spelling you use. After each take, Hebrish replaces what the model wrote with your spelling. It corrects the text; it doesn\'t change what the model hears, so it fixes words the model gets wrong the same way each time. Applies from your next take.
Shared with Android\'s personal dictionary: words you add here appear in your keyboards, and words you add in a keyboard (Add to dictionary) work here.

Android only shares its personal dictionary with apps that are an enabled keyboard. Turn on the Hebrish voice keyboard (you don\'t have to use it) to share this list with your other keyboards. Until then, Hebrish uses the words you add here.

Android only shares its personal dictionary with apps that are an enabled keyboard, and the Hebrish voice keyboard is off. Hebrish is using the words you add here and its copy of Android\'s list from %1$s.
Word, as it should be written
Heard as (optional): what Hebrish writes instead
For example Hebrish, heard as \"hebrew ish\". Leave it empty to fix only the spelling and capitals of a word Hebrish already hears. Android keeps it as the word\'s shortcut.
Added %1$s, also to Android\'s personal dictionary
Remove %1$s? It is also removed from Android\'s personal dictionary, so from your other keyboards.
This phone has no personal dictionary screen in Settings.

A word matches with any capitals, and a word of four or more letters also when the model splits it (git hub, Git-Hub → GitHub). A word you write all in lower case keeps a capital at the start of a sentence. Every match is replaced: adding IT turns every \"it\" into IT.
